text:
marta: Quick heads-up — planning to publish py/ts SDK 3.8.0-rc1 in tonight's change window (23:00 UTC). Will include the async client split and a soft deprecation notice for legacy sync client. Please read and ack if you have blockers.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled by marta for 2026-03-21 23:00 UTC -> staging then canary (cohort=10%). CI: build=passed, integ-tests=flaky (1 failing test).

leo: Re: flaky integ test — which test is failing? if it's the auth flow we should hold.

marta: The failing test is auth/refresh-token-handoff — appears intermittent on macos-latest. Not seen on linux runners. I'm inclined to proceed but gate production canary behind extra smoke (auth refresh + e2e).

jess: Recommend pinning the current stable (3.7.4) on the dist-tag "stable" and publish rc under "next"/"rc". If canary fails, auto-roll back to 3.7.4 using dist-tag swap.

sam: Also need to coordinate credential rotation note in release notes. We changed the default KMS key name for private deploys — customers with pinned creds might need an extra step. Add a short migration snippet in the docs and link in the notes.

raul: +1 on docs. Who's owner for release notes? I can draft the deprecation blurb for sync client and the migration snippet for KMS.

marta: @raul please draft release notes. @jess I'll do the dist-tag pin rules in the publish script. @leo can you do an auth smoke run in staging after the canary is up?

leo: Yep. I'll run the smoke script and put results here. Quick note: can we make the canary cohort 5% instead of 10% for this one? less blast radius while flaky test exists.

jess: 5% sounds fine. Also setting rollback criteria: error rate >0.5% on auth endpoints OR any auth-refresh e2e failures -> immediate revert. Documented in the publish playbook.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started (cohort=5%). Jobs: publish-py, publish-ts, update-dist-tags. Logs: publish-py -> success, publish-ts -> success, update-dist-tags -> queued.

marta: Running the distribution tag update now: will push 3.8.0-rc1 to "next" and ensure "stable" remains at 3.7.4. Also updating CHANGELOG.md snippet.

deploy-bot: update-dist-tags -> success. Canaries are receiving traffic. Observability: 10m window for initial metric check.

leo: Ran auth-smoke against canary endpoints: auth token refresh OK, no failures in 30m. Latency within expected bounds. Sending results to #observability.

sam: Docs note drafted and pushed to docs repo: https://git.internal/docs/sdk/migration-kms.raft (PR 542). Please review quick.

raul: Release notes draft: 
- Breaking/changed: async client becomes primary. Legacy sync client marked deprecated (will be removed in v4.0).
- Migration: small snippet for credential KMS change and how to rebind keys.
- Backwards compat: examples for both py and ts.
PR: https://git.internal/release-notes/3.8.0-rc1

marta: LGTM. Two operational checks before promoting to GA: (1) 1h canary window with auth e2e clean, (2) docs + release-notes published. If either fails -> rollback.

deploy-bot: Canary 1h checkpoint reached. Metrics summary: overall 0.07% error rate (below threshold), auth e2e passed, no elevated latency.

jess: Given metrics, I'm comfortable promoting to staged GA next window. One ask: mark npm dist-tag for TS as "rc-3.8.0" and leave "latest" untouched. For Py, keep wheel/twine uploads under "next".

marta: Agreed. We'll schedule GA publish for tomorrow's 02:00 UTC quiet window. For now closing the RC thread. Thanks everyone — please keep an eye on customers flagged in the release watchlist. :shipit:

leo: acked.

jess: ack.

sam: ack.

marta: Final note — if we see post-promote auth regressions, we'll revert dist tags and run emergency hotfix release flow (see playbook link).
